title: Trump eyes $100,000 OPT fee
summary_en: The Trump administration is reportedly weighing a plan to fix a $100,000 fee onto America’s post-graduation employment program for international students known as Optional Practical Training (OPT).
author: Polly Nash

title: UK universities urged to diversify Sub-Saharan Africa strategies
summary_en: UK universities have been told to think broadly about new TNE opportunities and diversified recruitment models in Sub-Saharan Africa, as tighter compliance rules and policy changes reshape student mobility.
author: Polly Nash

title: Kaplan International Languages to rebrand as Positively Languages
summary_en: Kaplan International Languages will rebrand as Positively Languages later this year following its acquisition by private equity firm Inspirit Capital, signalling a new direction for the company.
author: Beth Kennedy
title_cn: Kaplan International Languages to rebrand as Positively Languages

title: Australian MP Julian Hill on public good vs private profit, visa refusals and value
summary_en:
At The PIE Live Asia Pacific, 
Julian Hill defended the Australian government’s focus on integrity and managed growth, argued Australia can extract more value from a similar number of international students, and offered a candid comparison between public universities and private providers.
author: Kim Martin
title_cn: Australian MP Julian Hill on public good vs private profit, visa refusals and value

title: “We’ve lost 20 years of growth”: Australian ELICOS and VET sectors hit out at visa policy
summary_en: Australian sector leaders at a major industry event have hit out against record high visa denials and government efforts to achieve “managed growth” for damaging the English language and vocational education sectors.
author: Polly Nash

title: Australia’s visa “quality correction” leaves sector seeking greater certainty

title_cn: Australia’s visa “quality correction” leaves sector seeking greater certainty

title: ‘Not an Australia alternative’: New Zealand’s international ed sector is going for growth
summary_en: New Zealand is charging ahead with its plans to increase international enrolments, stressing its desirability as a study destination in its own right rather than as a substitution for nearby Australia.
author: Beth Kennedy

title: US ELT hit by 14% student drop and shorter stays
summary_en: The number of students on English language programs in the US declined by 14% in 2025, as experts highlight the knock-on impact on higher education and communities across the country.
author: Polly Nash
title_cn: US ELT hit by 14% student drop and shorter stays

title: The PIE Live Asia Pacific 2026: Insights from Julian Hill MP
summary_en: Speaking at The PIE Live Asia Pacific, Hill tackles social licence and market concentration, warning that when 60–70% of students come from one country it’s bad for student experience, social licence, soft power and business risk. He also points to recent government action including the suspension of new VET/ELICOS entrants and and argues that the sector has largely backed these measures.
author: The PIE News team
title_cn: The PIE Live Asia Pacific 2026: Insights from Julian Hill MP

title: Most NOSCs stay flat as Australia releases 2027 provider numbers
summary_en: Australia has published indicative provider-level allocations for 2027, with public universities largely retaining their previous allocations while other higher education providers receive recalculated allocations under a revised methodology.
